diagnosis_summary: Rock confirmed and closed this issue with commit c83705a08d2df6977c158c027e9cf3bb45d5371e and recorded the fix in the v19.3 release notes. Registration Entry created or renewed a RegistrationSession for redirect payment flows, then compared the registration's full non-wait-list count with only the instance's remaining capacity. An existing registration at capacity was therefore treated as requesting its already-held spots again. The fix credits saved, non-wait-list, non-temporary registrants and checks only a true increase; new registrations and additional spots remain capacity-limited.
workaround_summaries: Upgrade to a package proven to contain the capacity-credit fix. Before upgrade, use an approved staff payment or follow-up path for an already-registered person who cannot reach a redirect gateway. Do not increase capacity, move wait-list state, duplicate a registration, or edit payment records solely to bypass the error.

verification_playbook.goal: Determine whether the installed Registration Session service credits already-reserved spots and whether active full registrations create exposure, without starting a payment or changing registration data.
prerequisites: Know the exact installed Rock version or build ancestry.
Have read-only access to aggregate registration-capacity data and gateway configuration.

steps.title: Check build ancestry
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the installed package contains commit c83705a08d2df6977c158c027e9cf3bb45d5371e or equivalent logic that credits saved active registrants when the session count represents the full existing registration.
steps.expected_if_affected: The Registration Entry flow passes the full registration count into capacity validation without crediting already-reserved active spots.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: The installed flow credits saved non-wait-list spots and limits only the requested increase.

steps.title: Count active full or over-capacity instances
steps.instructions: Return only an aggregate count. Do not return instance names, IDs, registrants, balances, gateways, or payment details.
steps.probe: SELECT COUNT(*) AS ActiveFullOrOverCapacityInstanceCount FROM [RegistrationInstance] ri WHERE ri.[IsActive] = 1 AND ri.[MaxAttendees] IS NOT NULL AND ri.[MaxAttendees] > 0 AND ri.[MaxAttendees] <= (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM [RegistrationRegistrant] rr INNER JOIN [Registration] r ON r.[Id] = rr.[RegistrationId] WHERE r.[RegistrationInstanceId] = ri.[Id] AND rr.[OnWaitList] = 0 AND r.[IsTemporary] = 0)
steps.expected_if_affected: The count is greater than zero and the installed build lacks the fix, establishing possible exposure without proving an outstanding redirect payment exists.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: The count is zero, or the installed build contains the corrected capacity-credit logic.
evidence_to_record: aggregate active full or over-capacity instance count

steps.title: Inspect redirect-payment exposure
steps.instructions: Without beginning a payment or saving configuration, determine whether any active full instance allows outstanding balances and uses a gateway that redirects outside Rock. Record only yes or no, not instance, gateway, account, or registrant details.
steps.expected_if_affected: At least one full instance has an existing balance flow through an external redirect gateway on a build without the fix.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: No such configuration exists, or the installed build contains the fix.
evidence_to_record: external redirect exposure present yes or no

limitations: The aggregate capacity count does not identify outstanding balances or gateway behavior and must not be treated as proof that a registrant encountered the error.
Do not reproduce the payment flow in production; a full end-to-end test belongs in an isolated environment with a test gateway.

context.scope: existing registrations completing payment through a redirect gateway at or over capacity
exact Registration Entry and Registration Session capacity revision
official release-note fix; verify exact package inclusion
